newsitem.title: USA: Airbus says opposes exclusive purchase agreements.
newsitem.headline: Airbus says opposes exclusive purchase agreements.

text.p: Airbus Industrie said Tuesday that it will not consider exclusive purchase agreements with airlines, altering comments made by a company spokeswoman last week.
"Airbus Industrie will not enter into exclusivity agreements," the consortium's statement said. "The legality of such deals are for appropriate authorities to determine and not for Airbus Industrie."

European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has made exclusive provider relationships between Boeing and two American carriers -- Delta Air Lines Inc and AMR Corp's American Airlines -- a central issue in the proposed merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.
"To our mind this (exclusive agreements) is something which should be declared illegal," Van Miert told Reuters last month during a visit to Washington.
Interviewed by Reuters on May 22, the Airbus spokeswoman was asked whether airbus would agree to exclusive provider agreements.
"Airbus will always try to fill market demand," the spokeswoman said. Did that mean, she was asked, that Airbus would agree to its own exclusive provider agreement?
"We would consider it seriously." In that case, she was asked, what did Airbus think about the Boeing exclusive provider deals?
"We do obviously object to the exclusive deals - we think they're anti-competitive - but so far they're not against the law," the spokeswoman said.
In a press release Tuesday, headlined, "Airbus Industrie Corrects Erroneous News Report," the company said:
"The spokesperson quoted in last week's news item did not state Airbus Industrie's position clearly enough or was misunderstood by the reporter."
